_meta.description: Runnable-tool manifest for litrun.py. Commands verified against upstream READMEs/PyPI (2025-2026). Star counts and the full 70+ catalog live in ../reference/catalog.md; only tools that can be installed & driven programmatically are listed here.

tools.name: MinerU
tools.notes: PDF/Office/image -> LLM-ready Markdown/JSON. No API key. GPU optional; add '-b pipeline' for CPU-only. ~16GB RAM recommended.

tools.name: marker
tools.notes: Fast PDF/doc -> Markdown/JSON. No key for base use; '--use_llm' boost needs an LLM key (e.g. GOOGLE_API_KEY). Pulls in PyTorch; GPU recommended. Use 'marker <dir>' for batch.

tools.name: docling
tools.notes: IBM document parser -> Markdown/JSON/HTML. No API key. Accepts local paths or URLs. Optional VLM pipeline: 'docling --pipeline vlm --vlm-model granite_docling <src>'.

tools.name: PaperQA2
tools.example: pqa ask 'What methods does this corpus use?'
tools.notes: Citation-backed RAG QA. Run pqa from a directory containing your PDFs. Needs an LLM key (OpenAI by default; Anthropic/Gemini/local Ollama also supported). Python 3.11+.

tools.name: ASReview LAB
tools.notes: Active-learning screening for PRISMA/systematic reviews. 'asreview lab' launches a local web UI in the browser. Imports CSV/RIS/XLSX. No API key, no GPU. Python 3.10+.

tools.name: GPT Researcher
tools.example: python -c "import asyncio; from gpt_researcher import GPTResearcher; r=GPTResearcher(query='YOUR TOPIC'); asyncio.run(r.conduct_research()); print(asyncio.run(r.write_report()))"
tools.notes: Async deep-research library (no console script). Needs BOTH OPENAI_API_KEY and TAVILY_API_KEY. For the web UI, clone the repo and run 'python -m uvicorn main:app --reload'.

ui.notes: FastAPI + web frontend. Reads keys from a .env in the repo root (litrun writes it for you). Serves at :8000.

tools.name: STORM / Co-STORM
tools.example: See repo examples/ — instantiate STORMWikiRunner with an LM + retriever, then runner.run(topic=..., do_research=True, do_generate_article=True)
tools.notes: Wikipedia-style survey generator (library). Needs an LLM key AND a retriever key (YDC_API_KEY from You.com, or Bing). Runnable demos + Streamlit UI live in the cloned repo's examples/frontend.

ui.notes: Streamlit demo (frontend/demo_light). Enter your OpenAI + You.com (YDC) keys in the app's sidebar / secrets. Serves at :8501.

tools.name: scholarly
tools.example: python -c "from scholarly import scholarly; print(next(scholarly.search_author('Steven A Cholewiak')))"
tools.notes: Google Scholar client (library). No key, but Scholar blocks bare IPs on search_pubs/citedby — you typically need a proxy (built-in ProxyGenerator / ScraperAPI).

tools.name: pyalex
tools.example: python -c "import pyalex; pyalex.config.email='you@example.com'; from pyalex import Works; print(Works()['W2741809807']['title'])"
tools.notes: OpenAlex API client (library). Set pyalex.config.email for the polite pool. As of ~2026 OpenAlex asks for an API key for higher limits: pyalex.config.api_key='...'.

tools.name: arXiv search & download
tools.notes: Bundled fetcher (uses the free 'arxiv' package). Searches arXiv and downloads PDFs + a manifest.json into --outdir. No API key. Query supports cat:, AND/OR. Feeds retrieval workflows into PaperQA2.

tools.name: arxiv-mcp-server
tools.notes: MCP server (stdio) to search/download/analyze arXiv. Runs via uvx (no install needed). Registered in an MCP client, not queried directly.

tools.name: paper-search-mcp
tools.notes: MCP server to search/download across 20+ sources (arXiv, PubMed, bioRxiv, S2, OpenAlex...). Set an Unpaywall email for OA lookups. Verify exact optional env-var names in the README before relying on them.

tools.name: zotero-mcp
tools.notes: MCP server bridging your Zotero library. Easiest: after install run 'zotero-mcp setup' to auto-write the client config. Local mode (ZOTERO_LOCAL=true) needs the Zotero desktop app running with the local API enabled; Web API mode needs ZOTERO_API_KEY + ZOTERO_LIBRARY_ID.
